cells.tense: You are in the middle of the exchange, adjusting it as it goes.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are carrying that is not yours to keep giving, and hand it back today.
cells.core:
Someone gives, you give back, and you keep checking the weight on both sides as you do it. That checking is not fuss — it is what keeps the thing alive between you. You can feel when something lands right and when it lands heavy, and you stop mid-sentence to recalibrate. Not many people stay in contact at that level of attention.

What this looks like when it is running clean: you give from what you actually have and let receiving happen without rushing to square it. Keeping it there costs you something. You stay in contact when it would be easier to go quiet, and you do not always get thanked for it. You are already paying that price.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the exchange alive by staying in contact.
cells.verb: giving and receiving in even exchange
cells.place: where you keep adjusting the balance between yourself and others

cells.tense: You are working out the terms of an exchange that has not happened yet.
cells.ask: Let the next favour come in without repaying it today.
cells.core:
Before anyone asks, you have counted what you owe and what you are owed, and the counting has become the relationship. It looks like fairness, and it is really you bracing against a bill that has not arrived. The bracing takes more out of you than the bill ever would.

Holding on through pressure is not the same as keeping every account level. It is carrying what is real without crushing it or yourself. When this is running clean, you have a plain sense of what is right and you do not have to run the numbers to trust it. Today the numbers are the ones talking.

cells.tense: You stopped putting things into the exchange a while back.
cells.ask: Offer one small thing to one person, and let it stand without an answer.
cells.core:
Your hands came off the arrangement, and now you watch from a step away. What you have to give is not gone — it just has nowhere to land at the moment, and you have stopped looking for a way in.

What sharpens this again is attention, not effort. Notice one place where something is being offered and you are not taking it. Notice where you are owed and are not saying so. Running clean, this looks like seeing the shape of the exchange clearly without forcing anything through it. That kind of seeing is already yours. Put it on one small thing this week and let it move.
cells.sheetLine: You took your hands off, and the exchange went quiet.

cells.tense: You are already moving fairness around between people without saying so.
cells.ask: Say out loud one thing you deliberately evened out for someone this week.
cells.core:
You soften one person's load and quietly take it back later in another room. By the time anyone notices, the adjustment is done, and you call it just how things are. No one has seen you do it, including you.

The sense underneath is sound — you feel what is fair before you can explain it, and you have learned to keep that feeling to yourself. That habit is older than it needs to be. Running clean, you know what is right and you say it plainly, without building a case first. The fairness is yours. Only the credit has been parked somewhere else, and it is waiting.
cells.sheetLine: You even things out quietly and call it nothing.
